items.title: Bayesian Multiclass Segmentation for Remote Sensing: Integrating User Priors and Uncertainty
items.description: Geospatial object segmentation from aerial imagery is a significant task in remote sensing, underpinning a wide range of applications such as environmental monitoring, urban planning, and defense. Despite advances in deep learning (DL), conventional segmentation methodologies often suffer from limited generalizability due to regional variability, data distribution shifts, and ambiguous object boundaries. Moreover, most existing approaches are based on static, pretrained architectures with the lack of adaptability to unseen domains or user-specific requirements. To alleviate this, we introduce, in this study, a novel interactive segmentation framework that integrates few-shot semionline adaptation with a Bayesian variational inference mechanism. Our approach dynamically incorporates user corrections and convolutional feature representations to construct an adaptive prior within a variational autoencoder (VAE), thereby enabling user knowledge and feedback to be directly encoded into the segmentation process. This probabilistic formulation enhances the iterative refinement of segmentation masks in response to user input and enables principled quantification of model uncertainty, which is a strong factor for trustworthy deployment in real-world geospatial applications. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark remote sensing datasets demonstrate that our method achieves superior segmentation accuracy and robustness with minimal user intervention, outperforming existing test-time adaptation (TTA) and interactive segmentation techniques. The proposed framework represents a scalable and user-adaptive solution, bridging the gap between automated segmentation and domain-expert guidance, and advancing the state of the art in geospatial analysis for heterogeneous and dynamic environments.

items.title: Geometric Representation of Wet Snow Through a Tricontinuous Random Composite and Its Scattering Characterization With the Discrete Dipole Approximation
items.description: Building upon the previously developed bicontinuous random medium model for dry snow, this study presents an enhanced electromagnetic scattering model for wet snow, incorporating explicit treatment of water morphology. The model distinguishes among ice, water, and air phases, and further separates liquid water into discrete droplets and continuous water films through morphological thresholds during structural generation. To analyze the electromagnetic scattering behavior of this three-phase medium, the discrete dipole approximation (DDA) method is employed to solve the volume integral equations. The feasibility of the DDA approach to characterize wet snow scattering is examined. This work then investigates the scattering properties and the effective permittivity of the random media composites at 37 GHz, considering variations in structural parameters, water content, and water morphology. This study further examines how these variations influence the brightness temperatures and backscatter coefficients arising from a wet snow layer. Model performance is then evaluated at Ku band and Ka band through comparisons with field observations from the Nordic Snow Radar Experiment (NoSREx) 2011 campaign, enabling validation for both active and passive microwave simulations, respectively. The wet snow electromagnetic scattering model developed in this article directly links the wet snow microstructure to its scattering behaviors, and it provides valuable insights for enhancing microwave remote sensing capabilities in snow-covered regions.

items.title: Cloud, Atmospheric Radiation and Renewal Energy Application (CARE) Version 1.2 Shortwave Cloud Radiative Forcing From Himawari-8 and FY-4A: Algorithm Development and Preliminary Validation
items.description: Clouds strongly modulate the radiation balance of the Earth and the atmosphere system by reflection of shortwave radiation and absorption of longwave radiation. In this study, we develop a shortwave cloud radiative effect (SWCRE) algorithm for the cloud, atmospheric radiation, and renewal energy application (CARE) datasets (Version 1.2) from geostationary satellites of Himawari-8/9 and FY-4A. First, the lookup tables (LUTs) for retrieval of cloud optical thickness (COT) and cloud effective radius (CER) (LUTs-A), and shortwave radiation at the surface and TOA (LUTs-B) were generated by the radiative transfer model (RSTAR). Second, COT and CER for water and ice clouds were retrieved based on the LUT method with LUTs-A, respectively. Third, shortwave radiation at the surface and TOA were estimated under assumptions with clouds (all-sky) and without clouds (clear-sky). Finally, an SWCRE at the surface and TOA was estimated based on the difference between all- and clear-sky shortwave radiation. Validations of SWCRE from Himawari-8 against the five years (2016–2020) Clouds and the Earth’s Radiant Energy System (CERES) product show high accuracy with root-mean-squared error (RMSE) of 5.5 and 4.6 Wm−2 at the surface and TOA, respectively; R values of 0.96 and 0.97. High accuracy, spatial–temporal resolutions of CARE SWCRE products can be further used for Earth’s radiation balance study.

items.title: Spectral-Fidelity-Preserving Recalibration of Reflective Solar Bands for MERSI-II Onboard Fengyun-3D Satellite
items.description: Since its 2017 launch, the Medium-Resolution Spectral Imager-II (MERSI-II) aboard the China Fengyun-3D (FY-3D) polar-orbiting satellite has delivered global observations of the atmosphere, oceans, and terrestrial vegetation, yet its reflective solar bands (RSBs) exhibit gradual on-orbit radiometric degradation and temporal fluctuations. We introduce a new spectral-fidelity-preserving (SFP) cross-calibration framework that uses AQUA/moderate resolution imaging spectroradiometer (MODIS) as the reference. Unlike conventional approaches that homogenize spectral responses, the SFP model explicitly retains MERSI-II’s intrinsic spectral observation characteristics while correcting radiometric bias. When applied to FY-3D/MERSI-II observations (January 2018–March 2025), the seven recalibrated RSBs achieve a mean relative bias near 1% and a 2%–3% improvement relative to the operational calibration coefficients, remaining stable throughout the 7-year record. Mann–Kendall (MK) tests identify distinct degradation breakpoints, with B05 ( $1.38~\mu $ m) and B06 ( $1.64~\mu $ m) changing earlier around October 2021, and other bands fluctuating after May 2024. We also produce daily calibration coefficients, substantially improving upon current monthly or semiannual updates. The related algorithm and daily calibration coefficients are publicly released on GitHub to support community uptake and operational use.

items.title: High-Resolution Spatiotemporal Estimation of PM2.5 in Complex Terrain During the Heating Period: A Case Study in Shanxi, China
items.description: High-resolution particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter  $\le$  $ 2.5$   $\mu $ m (PM2.5) monitoring during heating periods in complex terrains is essential for public health and pollution control. Conventional ground-based observation stations suffer from spatial sparsity, while aerosol optical depth (AOD)-derived PM2.5 estimations are inherently limited by atmospheric correction and data coverage. Bypassing these limitations, our methodology innovatively develops two deep neural network (DNN) architectures—residual DNN (Res-DNN) and concatenation DNN (Con-DNN)—through direct fusion of top of atmosphere reflectance (TOA) with normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), meteorological data, and digital elevation model (DEM) data. Evaluated via ten-fold cross-validation (CV), the Con-DNN model achieved superior performance root mean squared error (RMSE):  $11.35~\mu $ g/m3, mean absolute percentage error (MAPE): 27.12%, R2: 0.92), Res-DNN and Con-DNN reducing RMSE by 4.10% and 7.04%, respectively, compared to the baseline DNN. SHAP-based interpretability analysis reveals that TOA data are the primary drivers of PM2.5 estimation, contributing 50.6% and 42.8% to the model during the heating and nonheating periods, respectively. TOA-driven models outperformed AOD-PM2.5 models in coverage and temporal resolution. Spatial analysis indicates that PM2.5 hotspots mainly correlate with topography and human activities, predominantly occurring in topographical depressions and anthropogenically intensive zones. During heating periods, morning PM2.5 hotspots frequently form in northern and southern Shanxi. Afternoon increases in ground wind speed partially improve air quality there. However, persistent pollution occurs in central Taiyuan Basin where weak winds and basin topography trap pollutants.

items.title: Latent Space Transformer for High-Resolution Particulate Matter Nowcasting From LiDAR Observations
items.description: Accurate forecasting of particulate matter distribution, particularly the occurrence and evolution of extreme pollution events, is essential for environmental monitoring and public health response. However, most existing approaches rely on mesoscale observations from in situ monitoring stations or satellites, which lack the spatial resolution necessary to capture fine-grained local variations in pollutant levels. To address this challenge, we utilize quantum-enhanced aerosol LiDAR observations with decameter-scale spatial resolution to derive a particulate matter index (PMI), which quantifies the atmospheric extinction coefficient and local pollutant concentrations. Building upon this, we propose a comprehensive deep learning (DL) framework for PMI nowcasting, comprising a vector-quantized variational autoencoder (VQ-VAE) for learning latent space representations, and a Transformer-based forecaster for predicting future PMI distributions. The integration of the vector quantization technique enables substantial data compression by removing pixel-level redundancies while preserving essential high-level features. To further enhance the model’s sensitivity to extreme pollution episodes, we introduce a magnitude-exponentiated weighted square error (MEWSE) loss function, which prioritizes accurate reconstruction in regions with elevated PMI values. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our model significantly outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) baselines in forecasting the spatial distribution of extreme particulate matter concentrations, achieving up to 28% and 24% improvements in CSI over ResNet at thresholds of 0.20 and 0.30, respectively. In the future, this DL framework may be extended to forecasting other meteorological phenomena exhibiting similarly skewed spatial distributions, such as extreme precipitation or marine heatwaves, across diverse remote sensing platforms.

items.title: Deep Learning for Clouds and Cloud Shadow Segmentation in Methane Satellite and Airborne Imaging Spectroscopy
items.description: Effective cloud and cloud shadow detection is a critical prerequisite for accurate retrieval of concentrations of atmospheric methane (CH4) or other trace gases in hyperspectral remote sensing. This challenge is especially pertinent for MethaneSAT, a satellite mission launched in March 2024, to fill a significant data gap in terms of resolution, precision, and swath between coarse-resolution global mappers and fine-scale point-source imagers of methane, and for its airborne companion mission, MethaneAIR. MethaneSAT delivers hyperspectral data at an intermediate spatial resolution ( $\sim{\!}{\!} 100 \times 400$  m), whereas MethaneAIR provides even finer resolution (~25 m), enabling the development of highly detailed maps of concentrations that enable quantification of both the sources and rates of emissions. In this study, we use machine learning methods to address the cloud and cloud shadow detection problem for sensors with these high spatial resolutions. Cloud and cloud shadows in remote sensing data need to be effectively screened out as they bias methane retrievals in remote sensing imagery and impact the quantification of emissions. We deploy and evaluate conventional techniques—including iterative logistic regression (ILR) and multilayer perceptron (MLP)—with advanced deep learning architectures, namely, U-Net and a spectral channel attention network (SCAN) method. Our results show that conventional methods struggle with spatial coherence and boundary definition, affecting the detection of clouds and cloud shadows. Deep learning models substantially improve detection quality: U-Net performs best in preserving spatial structure, while SCAN excels at capturing fine boundary details. Notably, SCAN surpasses U-Net on MethaneSAT data, underscoring the benefits of incorporating spectral attention for satellite-specific features. In addition, we combine the predictions of both U-Net and SCAN through a convolutional neural network (CNN). This ensemble method achieves the best performance on both MethaneAIR ( $F1$ :  $78.50~\pm ~3.08$ %) and MethaneSAT ( $F1$ :  $78.80~\pm ~1.28$ %) datasets, representing improvements of 2% and 10% over conventional methods (U-Net:  $78.50~\pm ~3.08$ % and  $68.56~\pm ~0.36$ %  $F1$ , respectively), while maintaining efficient inference (4.1 ms per 1000 km2). This in-depth assessment of various disparate machine learning techniques, as applied to MethaneSAT and MethaneAIR imaging spectroscopic data at varying spatial resolutions, demonstrates the strengths and effectiveness of advanced deep learning architectures in providing robust, scalable solutions for clouds and cloud shadow screening toward enhancing methane emission quantification capacity of existing and next-generation hyperspectral missions. Our data and code are publicly available at: https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/IKLZOJ

items.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Observation Station Placement Optimization for Ocean Monitoring
items.description: Ocean observation underpins our understanding of marine dynamics. Given the high cost of deploying and maintaining observation stations, optimizing their placement is essential for accurate ocean field reconstruction. Here, we propose RL-SPO, a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based framework for station placement optimization. The framework autonomously learns optimal placement strategies through closed-loop interactions with a reconstruction-driven simulation environment, enabling sequential decision-making in complex spatial domains. It integrates three key innovations: an image-based state representation to capture spatial correlations, dynamic action masking to strictly enforce feasibility constraints, and environment-specific reward calibration to balance heterogeneous objectives. Experiments using satellite and reanalysis datasets from the Northwest Pacific Ocean show that RL-SPO consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in reconstructing temperature and salinity fields, and generalizes effectively across single- and multiobjective tasks in both 2-D and 3-D settings. Notably, RL-SPO reveals that optimal observation stations cluster in dynamically active, high-entropy regions such as coastal waters and the Kuroshio Extension, highlighting its ability to identify “informational hotspots” of the ocean system. Overall, RL-SPO provides a generalizable and data-driven paradigm for ocean observational network design, offering an efficient and cost-effective pathway toward intelligent ocean monitoring.

items.title: Shipborne Multisource Fusion Framework for Ocean Wave Inversion: Integrating X-Band Radar and Motion Data
items.description: Accurate perception of near-field waves is critical for the safety of ship navigation. Existing X-band radar inversion methods face dual constraints: spectral-analysis methods require buoy-assisted calibration, and data-driven approaches fail to achieve comprehensive wave parameter inversion. To overcome these limitations, this article proposes RaMoWave, a novel shipborne multisource fusion framework for ocean wave inversion. The key innovations include: 1) a generalized ship motion intelligent inversion model that extracts significant wave height (SWH) and spectral peak period under arbitrary wave encounter angles and 2) a feature fusion strategy that optimizes radar-derived wave spectra and reconstructs wave fields without relying on buoy data. Extensive validation via numerical simulations and sea trials [SWH: 0.5–5 m (simulation) and 0.5–2.4 m (sea trials)] demonstrates threefold superiority: 1) it enables comprehensive inversion of SWH, spectral peak period, characteristic period, and wave field—capabilities unattainable by existing intelligent approaches; 2) it achieves a 30% improvement in parameter inversion accuracy over spectral-analysis methods, with error reductions up to 50% in buoy-free scenarios; and 3) it maintains relative inversion errors below 7% across all scenarios, exhibiting superior applicability and robustness.

items.title: Maximum Wave Height Retrieval for GPM Satellites Based on Dynamic Correction
items.description: Operational satellite retrieval of the maximum wave height (EC-MWH) has long relied on linear wave theory, which estimates MWH as a fixed multiple of significant wave height (EC-SWH). This static approach fails to capture the dynamic nonlinearity of real ocean waves, leading to systematic biases. In this study, we introduce a novel physics-based method that synergistically uses active and passive microwave observations from the global precipitation measurement (GPM) mission to correct SWH dynamically and retrieve MWH directly. A dynamic correction factor is constructed from GPM microwave imager (GMI) brightness temperature—sensitive to wind induced energy input—and dual-frequency precipitation radar (DPR) radar backscatter—sensitive to wave steepness and nonlinear dissipation—thereby quantitatively diagnosing wave nonlinearity. Validated against 217 independent buoy observations, the proposed GPM MWH retrieval reduces the root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) by approximately 34% and 35%, respectively, compared to the ERA5 MWH product. This method demonstrates the feasibility of generating continuous, high-resolution global MWH fields, offering a new pathway toward the operational monitoring of extreme ocean waves from space.

items.title: A Comparative Analysis of Anti-Jamming Performance Between GPS-R and GAL-R Using Spaceborne DDM Data
items.description: The global navigation satellite system (GNSS)-based applications are highly vulnerable to radio frequency interference in GNSS bands (RFI-GB). Unfortunately, such interference currently occurs frequently worldwide. As a GNSS-based passive remote sensor, spaceborne GNSS reflectometry (GNSS-R) receivers inevitably suffer from terrestrial RFI-GBs (T-RFI-GBs). To investigate the anti-jamming performance differences between Global Positioning System (GPS) reflectometry (GPS-R) and Galileo reflectometry (GAL-R) on a global scale, this study first establishes a comparative model using FY-3F/GNOS-II delay–Doppler map (DDM) data and then validates it through a ground-based experimental platform. The main findings are as follows: 1) Europe, the Middle East, the Red Sea, and West Asia experience a high incidence of intense T-RFI-GBs, which significantly elevate the DDM noise floor, degrade the DDM peak signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and consequently reduce DDM availability rates for both systems through quality control (QC) filtering. 2) Globally, most intentional and unintentional L1-band T-RFI-GBs concentrate their power near the L1 center frequency. Owing to the split-spectrum characteristic of the binary offset carrier (BOC) modulation employed by GAL E1B signals, GAL-R demonstrates superior anti-jamming performance compared to GPS-R, generally resulting in higher DDM availability rates. In addition, GAL-R exhibits marginally better thermal noise resistance than GPS-R. 3) With the increasing worldwide prevalence of T-RFI-GBs, future implementations should consider adopting new-generation BOC-modulated signals such as L1C and B1C for GPS-R and BeiDou Satellite Navigation System (BDS) reflectometry (BDS-R) to improve their anti-jamming performance. 4) The different patterns in the noise part of affected DDMs, combined with their noise floor values, show potential for identifying T-RFI-GBs types and estimating their intensity.

items.title: Rethinking the Flow: A Canal-Based Machine Learning Approach to Urban Flood Detection
items.description: Machine learning (ML) methods have proven effective for mapping urban flood extents using remotely sensed data. However, the availability of suitable datasets remains a key challenge when training such models. Here, we present a novel approach to address this limitation. Instead of focusing on individual pixels, we use streets as the primary unit of analysis. This change allows us to use an entirely new type of ground-truth dataset: canal cities such as Venice, Italy. Here, we construct a reliable training dataset by labeling canals as flooded streets and regular streets as dry. We then use Sentinel-2 optical remote sensing data to develop an improved neural network architecture specifically designed to accurately classify canals and streets in complex urban environments: the custom street flood index (CSFI). Several other methods are evaluated, ranging from a simple normalized difference water index (NDWI) thresholding approach to more advanced ML techniques such as XGBoost, support vector machine (SVM), random forest, and neural networks. All advanced models yield promising results, significantly outperforming the classic NDWI baseline. However, among them, our new CSFI achieves the best performance, with an accuracy of 86% and a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 72% on our new training dataset. It also shows a strong ability to generalize to previously unseen cities. Finally, the new CFSI is tested on the real-world flood event of Porto Alegre, Brazil, in early May 2024, successfully mapping the extent of the urban flooding with 90% accuracy and an MCC of 70%. This makes our CSFI a new, efficient way to map flood extent at a street scale. The code is made available for users to apply the method to their own urban flood mapping needs.

items.title: A Novel Spectral Index for Mapping Sunflowers Using Sentinel-2 Imagery
items.description: As a globally significant oilseed and economic crop, accurately mapping the spatial distribution of sunflowers is crucial for ensuring food security. However, existing sunflower classification models are often complex in design, and specialized vegetation indices (VIs) remain relatively scarce. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop simple, efficient, and precise identification methods. This study introduces the sunflower identification index (SII), developed using the RE2 band, which is sensitive to chlorophyll variation, and the shortwave infrared 2 (SWIR2) band, which reflects differences in canopy water content. The SII provides critical spectral information necessary for distinguishing sunflowers from other crops. The effectiveness of the SII was evaluated in three major sunflower-producing countries—China, Ukraine, and France—across three representative sunflower-growing regions, each characterized by distinct climatic conditions and farming systems. The results indicate that in the Hetao Irrigation District (S1) in 2023, the classification accuracy of SII (overall accuracy (OA) = 94.39% and Kappa coefficient (Kappa) = 0.89) was significantly higher than that of the normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) and the green NDVI (GNDVI). Furthermore, the SII continued to exhibit excellent performance when applied across different years and regions (the Ukrainian site (S2) and Toulouse (S3) in 2022, S1 in 2021, and S3 in 2020). Finally, the SII was employed in binary classification using both the random forest (RF) and support vector machine (SVM) algorithms, yielding satisfactory results (OA > 90% and Kappa  $\ge 0.81$ ). These findings demonstrate that the SII possesses strong spatiotemporal transferability capabilities and robustness, allowing it to maintain high stability in complex and dynamic agricultural environments. In the future, integrating the SII with deep learning (DL) algorithms is expected to further enhance classification accuracy.

items.title: PanoEarth: Scaling Open-Vocabulary Panoptic Segmentation in Remote Sensing Images
items.description: Existing open-world remote sensing (RS) foundation models rely on text-to-image alignment for open-vocabulary semantic segmentation or object detection. However, semantic segmentation lacks instance-level delineation, while object detection fails to provide dense prediction for uncountable geographic features. Current approaches lack a unified solution for comprehensive panoptic understanding that jointly addresses semantic segmentation, instance segmentation, and object detection across all geographic elements. To bridge this gap, we propose PanoEarth, the first open-vocabulary panoptic segmentation framework for RS images, which integrates these tasks within a unified architecture. Our framework incorporates a scalable training strategy to compensate for missing background semantic information in instance segmentation data, enabling dense panoptic perception. Through the introduction of a domain-specific text embedding classifier to guide fine-tuning and establish precise mask query-to-category alignment, PanoEarth achieves competitive zero-shot open-vocabulary performance. We curate a large-scale panoptic dataset comprising 150k images spanning 111 geographic categories and millions of instances across landcover types, infrastructure elements, and fine-grained object subtypes. In zero-shot experiments, PanoEarth surpasses task-specific state-of-the-art models across multiple datasets and tasks. The joint co-training version enables unified extraction of 111 geographic categories, enabling hierarchical analysis from landcover mapping to fine-grained instance recognition. The source code is available at: https://github.com/xypu98/PanoEarth

items.title: Adaptive Photon Cloud Classification for Forest Canopies: A Multicriterion Approach With Spatially Aware Windowing
items.description: The Ice, Cloud, and Land Elevation Satellite-2 (ICESat-2)/Advanced Topographic Laser Altimeter System (ATLAS) offers unprecedented opportunities to generate geodetic elevation profiles of canopy heights and understory terrain. However, the ICESat-2 can only record the photon return position but cannot provide information on surface features. In view of that, to classify signal photons more accurately, this study proposes a fine photon classification algorithm based on the multicriterion spaceborne photon cloud classification approach using spatially aware windows (MCSP2C) for forested ecosystems. The proposed algorithm uses Gaussian functions, the kurtosis value, the number of degrees of freedom, and adaptive multiple criteria and provides the fine-classified ground, canopy photons, and the top canopy photons. The proposed method is verified by experiments, and the results indicate that compared with the conventional classification methods, the proposed MCSP2C method can achieve a better ground and canopy height classification accuracy in different application scenarios and has the advantage of parameter adaptation without manual intervention. The comparison results show that the R2 of the ground and canopy values obtained using the ICESat-2 photon data extracted by the proposed method is 0.97 and 0.76, and the mean root-mean-square error (RMSE) value in different study areas is 1.76 and 5.73 m, respectively. The results also demonstrate that the MCSP2C algorithm can achieve high-quality classification of the ICESat-2 photon data for forest canopy heights and understory terrains.

items.title: Spatial–Channel Selective State Space Models and Pruned Cross-Task Feature Transfer for Building Height Mapping From Aerial Images and DSMs
items.description: Building height mapping is widely coupled with footprint segmentation in a unified multitask learning (MTL) framework. In this study, we comprehensively explore the designs of the shared encoder, the bottleneck, and the decoders’ cross-task feature sharing in MTL for precise building height mapping, and propose Mamba-based building height estimation network (MBHNet). First, we discovered that Mamba, a state space model (SSM) variant with selective feature extraction capacity, is particularly suited for inferring building heights. However, in previous remote sensing (RS) related studies, only the global feature correlation capacity, the same as Transformer, is utilized. We design a local-then-global feature encoder, locally sensitive SSM (LS-SSM), which integrates neighborhood attention (NATTEN), input discriminant enhancer (IDE), and spatial-dimension selective SSM, ensuring rich local-to-global information extraction and strong adaptability for MTL tasks. Second, a channel-dimension selective SSM (CSSM)-based bottleneck is introduced to model interchannel dependencies, in which, unlike previous works, the channel-wise information is not compressed and fully preserved. Third, considering the redundancy of the commonly used full feature sharing strategy across different tasks, we develop a K-top relevant feature mining (KTM) strategy in the decoding stage to enable selective and pruned cross-task feature transfer. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that MBHNet consistently outperforms recent methods, achieving very significant relative gains of 12.7%, 32.7%/40.2%, and 32.8% in mean absolute error (MAE) for building height estimation on the GeoNRW dataset, Tainjin Test Set-I/II, and the ISPRS Potsdam dataset, respectively. The datasets used in this study will be made publicly available at: https://github.com/yudawen/MBHNet

items.title: AIG2AN: Ambiguous-Interpretation Generalized GAN for Self-Supervised Raster-Vector Semantic Segmentation for Cross-Modal Remote Sensing Image
items.description: Remote sensing image interpretation faces easily overlooked issues: 1) ambiguity: mutual occlusion between objects, e.g., buildings are occluded by trees and vice versa, which leads to ambiguity (building or tree) in GIS, and 2) expression conflicts: topology conflicts between the occluding and occluded objects. However, there have been no reports on the remote sensing ambiguous interpretation (RSAI) or its dataset (RSAID). To address these issues, an RSAID was built, and an ambiguous-interpretation generalized generative adversarial network (AIG2AN) with self-supervised raster-vector semantic segmentation for remote sensing images is proposed for the first time. With the occluding image generated, AIG2AN not only recognizes occlusion regarded as cheating but also restores the occluded semantic labels, which includes three modules: 1) random occlusion generator automatically generates the occluding image with the occluding and occluded labels for self-supervised learning with avoiding hallucination issue; 2) ambiguity dual-interpreters, including both occluding and occluded interpretations, is the first to be proposed; and 3) consistency contrastive learning module (C2LM) is to process the inconsistent interpretations in unambiguous region. Furthermore, we propose a novel multispectral cross-modal learning paradigm via self-supervised pseudo-labeling to automatically enhance the generalization of our AIG2AN in different sensor modalities, and propose a conflict-free and regularized raster-vector expression for interpretation results of ambiguous objects. Experiments on our manually restored RSAID from ISPRS Vaihingen and Potsdam show that AIG2AN improves mIoU and building IoU by 3.28% and 1.80%, with an ambiguity elimination index (AEI) of 85.32% and 76.41%, respectively. Moreover, we reveal the occlusion restoration mechanism. RSAID and code are available at: https://github.com/wenlailiu/AIG2AN

items.title: Development of a Hybrid SW-TES Method for Simultaneous Land Surface Temperature and Emissivity Retrieval From Landsat 8/9 Thermal Infrared Data
items.description: Land surface temperature (LST) is a widely recognized geophysical parameter for studying the interactions within the land-atmosphere system. Thermal infrared (TIR) remote sensing provides an unprecedented capability for retrieving LST accurately across scales from local landscapes to global coverage. After decades of development, numerous algorithms for recovering LST from spaceborne TIR measurements have been proposed. But either land surface emissivity (LSE) or atmospheric parameters were required in existing algorithms. Although the latest split window-temperature and emissivity separation (SW-TES) algorithm was stated to be able to estimate LST and LSE simultaneously without relying on any prior information, the implementation of this method suggests data acquisition from a minimum of three TIR channels. However, the operational Landsat 8/9 satellites are limited to two 11.0 and  $12.0~\mu $ m TIR channels, failing to separate LST and LSE simultaneously. To mitigate this issue, a two-channel-based SW-TES method was proposed here for direct LST and LSE retrieval from the Landsat 8/9 TIR measurements. Consequently, its performance was evaluated against in situ measured LSTs from the American surface radiation budget (SURFRAD) sites. Results revealed that the proposed method achieved an LST retrieval accuracy of about 1.88 and 2.17 K regarding Landsat 8 and Landsat 9 TIR data, even surpassing their official LST products with the accuracy of about 2.54 and 2.80 K. The LSE retrieval accuracy was evaluated via cross-validation with a discrepancy of <0.02. Therefore, conclusions can be drawn that the proposed approach is adequate to retrieve reliable LST from satellite measurements with just two TIR spectral bands. The findings are expected to be of great significance for generating the future LST products.

items.title: Moving Infrared Small Target Detection via Motion-Aided Integrated Spatial–Temporal Network
items.description: Moving infrared small target detection (MIRSTD) is crucial for various civilian applications. Motion information plays a key role in detecting and locating moving targets in complex infrared scenarios. Existing methods have primarily focused on designing and optimizing robust, complex 3-D spatial–temporal modules to process multiple consecutive input frames to extract motion information, yet they have largely overlooked the description of motion and optimization of input strategies, which limits their efficiency. In this work, we propose a novel motion-aided spatial–temporal integrated network (MIST-Net). We first optimize the input strategy by encoding the dominant motion characteristics across multiple consecutive frames using series expansion and temporal motion intensity analysis, thereby constructing a motion frame that consolidates motion information from several frames into one. The motion frame and target frame are then fed into the integrated network for extracting motion and spatial features, respectively. Additionally, to account for the mutual constraints and dependencies between motion and spatial information, we introduce a mutual calibration module (MCM) that refines the motion maps using spatial cues and enhances the spatial maps with motion information. To further improve the robustness of MIST-Net, we address the semantic gap between motion and spatial features by presenting a motion-spatial-coupled selective state space module (MSCM). Specifically, we generate a motion-spatial coupled state based on the mutual dependencies between the motion hidden state and spatial motion state using entropy theory. This coupled state dynamically adjusts the fusion of motion and spatial information. We conduct extensive experiments on the public SIRST and ITSDT-15K datasets, and the results demonstrate that MIST-Net outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods in both accuracy and speed.

items.title: Ivan-ISTD: Rethinking Cross-Domain Heteroscedastic Noise Perturbations in Infrared Small Target Detection
items.description: Infrared small target detection (ISTD) plays an important role in drone-based multimodality sensing. To address the dual challenges of cross-domain shift and heteroscedastic noise perturbations in ISTD, we propose a doubly wavelet-guided invariance learning framework (Ivan-ISTD). In the first stage, we generate training samples aligned with the target domain using wavelet-guided cross-domain synthesis. This wavelet-guided alignment machine accurately separates the target background through multifrequency wavelet filtering. In the second stage, we introduce real-domain noise invariance learning, which extracts real noise characteristics from the target domain to build a dynamic noise library. The model learns noise invariance through self-supervised loss, thereby overcoming the limitations of distribution bias in traditional artificial noise modeling. Finally, we create the dynamic-ISTD benchmark, a cross-domain dynamic degradation dataset that simulates the distribution shifts encountered in real-world applications. In addition, we validate the versatility of our method using other real-world datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of many quantitative metrics. In particular, Ivan-ISTD demonstrates excellent robustness in cross-domain scenarios. The code for this work can be found at: https://github.com/nanjin1/Ivan-ISTD

items.title: High-Fidelity GPR Diffraction Extraction via PSO-Guided Reflection Reconstruction in Wavelet-Dip Domains
items.description: Ground-penetrating radar (GPR) diffractions typically manifest weak responses resulting from electromagnetic wave interactions with subwavelength heterogeneities (e.g., cracks and voids) or geometric discontinuities (e.g., scattering edges and corners). These subtle yet informative wavefield components are critical for enabling enhanced illumination and dedicated imaging of subsurface microfeatures in infrastructure assessment and geological hazard mitigation. Current diffraction extraction methods in GPR face significant practical limitations: kinematic local-slope techniques are computationally intensive and may lead to loss of vertex events, whereas coherence analysis (CA) requires meticulous calibration of scaling factors and time-moveout corrections. Such constraints can compromise the resolution of imaging modalities, such as migration, tomography, and full-waveform inversion (FWI). To address these challenges, this study introduces an adaptive diffraction extraction workflow that integrates three core modules in wavelet and dip domains: a wavelet-based reflection model for structural preservation, dip-adaptive smoothing operators for wavefield decomposition, and particle swarm optimization (PSO) with multiobjective criteria (Laplacian sharpness, wavelet entropy (WE), and focusing metrics) for parameters optimization. The workflow iteratively extracts residual diffractions by optimizing wavelet decomposition levels, smoothing scales, and residual thresholds using PSO-driven fitness functions. Validated through the heterogeneous random media model, the Sigsbee2a benchmark, and field experiments, the PSO-guided workflow demonstrates quantifiable improvements in edge preservation, coherence artifacts reduction, spatial resolution, and kinematic consistency. By prioritizing the wavefield integrity and structural fineness, the proposed method provides refined inputs for subsequent imaging, highlighting its potential to advance the resolution and reliability of near-surface GPR sensing applications.

items.title: Deep Learning for Radargrammetric DSM Generation: A StereoSAR Dataset and Multiscale Fusion Network
items.description: Radargrammetry is an important technique for digital surface model (DSM) reconstruction, but accurate disparity estimation from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) stereo images remains challenging due to speckle noise and geometric distortions. Despite the success of deep learning in disparity estimation for stereo matching, its application in stereoscopic SAR (StereoSAR) is still limited due to the lack of high-quality training data and task-specific models. To address this issue, this study develops a deep learning framework for radargrammetric DSM generation, integrating dataset construction and a multiscale SAR stereo matching network. The StereoSAR4DSM dataset is developed using TerraSAR-X imagery and high-resolution aerial DSMs, with enhanced epipolar rectification and three SAR-driven augmentation strategies: multilooking variation, random pixel sampling, and random elevation perturbation. These strategies enrich data diversity and support robust deep learning model training. Based on this dataset, we design the multiscale StereoSAR fusion network (MSSFNet) that constructs pyramid cost volumes and progressively integrates multiscale cost information. An attention-guided fusion mechanism and a disparity refinement module further enhance matching accuracy and restore fine terrain structures. Experimental results on two test areas with different imaging modes demonstrate that the deep learning model trained with the StereoSAR4DSM dataset outperforms traditional approaches, and the proposed MSSFNet achieves the highest accuracy compared with other deep learning methods. In addition, comparative experiments show that the SAR-driven enhancement strategies significantly improve data diversity and lead to more accurate disparity estimation. Overall, these findings confirm the effectiveness of the proposed framework and highlight the potential of deep learning-based StereoSAR methods for efficient and accurate DSM reconstruction.

items.title: A Nonorthogonal Cartesian Fast BP Algorithm for High-Squint Spaceborne SAR Imaging
items.description: The Cartesian fast back projection (CFBP) algorithms are efficient, accurate, and applicable to multiple modes of spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging. However, in high-squint SAR configurations, these algorithms fail to achieve direct full-scene imaging due to degraded spectrum compression (SC). Although range partitioning can overcome this issue, it introduces additional complexity during the segmentation and combination processes. To address this limitation, this article proposes a nonorthogonal CFBP (NO-CFBP) algorithm by developing the concept of nonorthogonal signal processing. First, a 2-D nonorthogonal signal sampling method is proposed through spectrum analysis, revealing that the sampling frequency along one direction is determined by the bandwidth of another direction. On this basis, an optimal nonorthogonal Cartesian coordinate system (NOCCS) establishment method and a grid-interval setting criterion are proposed, ensuring effective SC across the entire scene with a minimal number of grid points. Furthermore, a new SC approach is derived to eliminate spectrum aliasing in subaperture images. Compared with the conventional CFBP algorithms, the proposed NO-CFBP algorithm not only eliminates the need for range partitioning but also significantly reduces grid points, leading to lower memory usage and higher computational efficiency. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified through both simulated and real data processing.

items.title: Semi-Supervised Learning-Based Permanent Scatterer Selection Method for GB-InSAR
items.description: Permanent scatterer (PS) selection is a critical step in ground-based interferometric synthetic aperture radar (GB-InSAR) measurements. Conventional methods, often constrained by empirical thresholds, demonstrate limited capability in selecting PSs within low-coherence regions caused by deformations. Deep learning provides a data-driven alternative to characterize PS features. However, PSs lack an absolute truth standard. Current deep learning-based PS selection methods predominantly employ fully supervised learning approaches, where significant label noise exists in the training sets. This interferes with the feature learning process of networks and consequently reduces PS recall rates. To overcome these limitations, this article proposes a semi-supervised learning-based PS selection method for GB-InSAR. By establishing a closed-loop optimization path of “refining the labels of training datasets and adjusting the strategy of model training,” this method suppresses the negative impact of label noise and enables the network to accurately fit the PS features, thus enhancing selection performance. First, initial reliable labels are generated via dual-threshold amplitude dispersion methods. Then, unlabeled pixels are processed through an optimal transport formulation solved via Sinkhorn–Knopp algorithm to improve label completeness. Finally, a mean teacher framework is introduced for semi-supervised training of the PS selection network, to systematically leverage implicit features of unlabeled data. A 3-D U-Net serves as the base network for pseudo-label generation and semi-supervised training, which processes sequential interferograms to output PS selection results. Simulated and measured datasets demonstrate the method’s superiority over fully supervised and conventional methods, which significantly increases PS density and quantity while ensuring quality, and it particularly exhibits superior performance in deformation regions.

items.title: Learning Modality Geometry for Multispectral Object Detection: Adaptive Spacing and 3-D Rotary Position Embedding
items.description: Positional encoding is crucial for the Transformer to effectively process multimodal feature information in multispectral object detection. However, existing studies often directly apply single-modal encoding designs to multimodal tasks, resulting in positional encoding focusing on spatial information while neglecting modality-specific information, which limits the performance of the Transformer. To explore the potential of positional encoding in jointly processing spatial and modality information in the multimodal domain, we propose an adaptive multimodal rotary position embedding transformer (AMRo-Former) for multispectral remote sensing object detection. It efficiently exploits multimodal spatial and modality information. The AMRo-Former consists of the multimodal rotary position embedding cross attention (MRoCA) and adaptive intermodal spacing module (AISM), where MRoCA includes multimodal rotary positional embedding (MRoPE) and cross-attention (CA) mechanism. We introduce a 3-D positional encoding strategy that addresses the challenges associated with 2-D positional encoding, particularly the difficulty of retaining modality-specific information. We design MRoPE by applying the 3-D positional encoding strategy and rotary position embedding (RoPE), which enables the independent processing of modality information through separate 2-D encoding and mixed 3-D encoding. Based on MRoPE, we further introduce MRoCA, the first multimodal attention mechanism to integrate a 3-D positional encoding strategy and to introduce the concept of intermodal spacing. To better exploit intermodal spacing while reducing the costs associated with manually setting, we design a lightweight AISM. Integrated into a dual-stream backbone network, our method achieved state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance in multispectral object detection, attaining the highest detection evaluation metrics to date on the vehicle detection in aerial imagery (VEDAI), drone-vehicle, and low-light vision infrared-visible paired (LLVIP) datasets, with mAP50 scores of 0.8962, 0.8531, and 0.9937. Overall, AMRo-Former demonstrates exceptional generalization performance in multispectral object detection.

items.title: Topology-Aligned Gated Interaction Network for Cross-Domain Hyperspectral Image Classification
items.description: Deep learning algorithms have shown great potential in the field of domain adaptation (DA) in unsupervised learning. However, in the task of cross-scene hyperspectral image (HSI) classification, current DA methods often focus only on local features or semantic information while ignoring the complementary relationship between the source and target domains. Thus, the cross-domain feature discrepancy limits the adaptation performance. To address these issues, we propose a novel topologically aligned gated interaction network (TAGIN) for cross-scene HSI classification. First, we introduce the bidirectional feature interaction network (BFIN), a novel framework in which convolutional neural network (CNN)-extracted local features dynamically interact with Transformer-derived semantic representations through a gating mechanism, forming dual-channel feature information. As a core part of BFIN, a cross-domain spectral space cross-attention (SSCA) mechanism is designed, combined with the bidirectional dynamic feature retention mechanism, to achieve adaptive feature fusion and cross-domain feature selection. Second, to achieve the feature alignment, we design a dynamic adaptive topology alignment loss, which is gradually optimized via memory enhancement and dynamic parameter adjustment mechanisms. Finally, we propose a topology-aware multiview consensus pseudo-label optimization (TA-MVCPO) strategy. High-confidence pseudo-labels are screened out through data augmentation samples, and then, the credibility of the pseudo-labels is verified through topological structure difference perception. The training model was fine-tuned based on high-confidence pseudo-labels, enhancing the adaptability of the training model to the target-domain data. The experimental results conducted on four cross-scenario HSI datasets demonstrate the superior performance of our proposed method.

items.title: HTDC: Hyperbolic Transformer With Dual-Momentum Contrastive Learning for Hyperspectral Anomaly Detection
items.description: Hyperspectral anomaly detection (HAD) remains a challenging task due to the complex spectral variability and spatial heterogeneity of real-world scenes. Reconstruction-based methods have been widely explored for deep learning-based HAD, but they rely on the assumption that background pixels can be faithfully reconstructed while anomalous pixels cannot. Although intuitive, this dichotomy oversimplifies the spectral–spatial characteristics of hyperspectral data and often fails in practice. In particular, when background regions exhibit strong variability or when anomalies share spectral similarities with their surroundings, reconstruction-based methods tend to generate false alarms and suffer from limited robustness. To overcome these limitations, this article moves beyond the reconstruction-based paradigm and proposes HTDC, a novel hyperbolic Transformer with a dual-momentum contrastive learning (DMCL) framework, which shifts the focus from background reconstruction to discriminative representation learning at both global and local levels. First, a custom-designed multiview data augmentation module generates complementary views from different perspectives, enriching spectral diversity and alleviating the limitations of contrastive learning (CL) under homogeneous samples. Second, a hyperbolic Transformer encoder exploits the hierarchical and structured nature of hyperspectral data, where hyperbolic geometry enables more effective attention aggregation than Euclidean space. Subsequently, a dual-momentum mechanism with dual temporal queues further stabilizes global learning while dynamically adapting to local changes, thereby mitigating sensitivity to class imbalance and spectral drift. Finally, in the detection stage, a sliding dual-window detection strategy with exponential mapping and guided filtering is employed to suppress background interference and enhance spatial contrast. Extensive experiments on multiple real hyperspectral images acquired by different sensors across various scenes demonstrate that the proposed HTDC consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in HAD tasks.

items.title: Fully Blind Hyperspectral Unmixing Without Explicit Mixing Models or Endmember Initialization
items.description: Autoencoder-based methods have gained prominence in blind hyperspectral unmixing (BHU), with most approaches based on predefined mixing assumptions, such as the linear mixing model (LLM). However, real-world scenes often involve complex nonlinear light-material interactions that are difficult to model explicitly, leading to systematic biases in endmember and abundance estimation when these assumptions deviate from the actual mixing mechanism. In this article, we extend conventional autoencoder-based BHU by jointly and adaptively learning the mixing mechanism directly from hyperspectral images (HSIs) while estimating endmembers and abundances, and propose a novel BHU framework termed unmixing Transformer (UNTR). In particular, an adaptive mixing mechanism modeling module is designed to parameterize the mixing mechanism, in which a specially designed transformer fuses heterogeneous endmember and abundance information. Furthermore, we develop an endmember query mechanism integrated into the adaptive mixing mechanism modeling module under a distribution alignment constraint, enabling robust endmember estimation under random initialization. As the first attempt to adaptively model the mixing mechanism as data-driven network parameters, UNTR achieves remarkable accuracy in both abundance and endmember estimation. Without relying on predefined mixing assumptions and well-initialized endmembers, UNTR exhibits strong adaptability to complex real-world scenarios. Our code will be available at https://github.com/Preston-Dong/UNTR

items.title: S2-Differential Feature Awareness Network for Hyperspectral Image Fusion
items.description: The fusion of hyperspectral image (HSI) and multispectral image (MSI) aims to fully exploit the complementary advantages of both modalities to generate a high-resolution HSI. However, existing HSI fusion methods fail to fully utilize frequency-domain information when capturing deep correlations between spectral bands, leading to difficulties in accurately preserving spatial texture details. Furthermore, these methods often overlook the intrinsic differential characteristics in HSI fusion, which easily causes spatial–spectral ( $S^{2}$ ) decoupling distortions. To address the aforementioned challenges, this article proposes a  $S^{2}$  differential feature awareness network (SSDAN) that employs a multiscale input strategy to fully preserve the rich spatial structures in the source images. Specifically, a spatial–frequency fusion network (SFFN) with a dual-branch architecture is designed to separately model multilevel spatial–frequency features of HSI and MSI, thereby effectively enhancing the joint representation of high-frequency details and global–local structures. In addition, we introduce a differential  $S^{2}$  complementarity module (DSSCM) that explicitly models modality-specific detailed features and adaptively aligns the dual-branch fused features with the shallow features, effectively mitigating decoupling distortions caused by feature mismatches. The code will be available at https://github.com/MSFLabX/SSDAN

items.title: An Information Entropy Feature Preservation-Based Band Selection and Noise Reduction Method for Hyperspectral Image Classification
items.description: Effectively reducing spectral redundancy while preserving the distinguishability of land cover is key to hyperspectral image classification (HSIC). Moreover, the presence of noise also interferes with the discriminability of spectral features. To address these issues, this article introduces a novel HSIC method that integrates band selection (BS) and discriminative feature extraction to achieve high performance of land-cover classification. First, by incorporating the concept of information entropy, the information entropy feature (IEF) is designed to describe the relationship between spectral bands, and then, the representative band group is selected based on the designed IEF. Second, a novel tensor subspace representation (TSR) model is proposed to separate the land cover of interest and noise component for the selected band group. Next, in light of different shapes and sizes exhibited by different land-cover, multiscale spatial–spectral features (MSFs) are used as supplementary information. Finally, the extracted class feature is used to guide and refine the extraction of land cover, further optimizing the classification performance. The results on multiple datasets show that the proposed method outperforms existing methods.

items.title: MCDB-Net: Multiview Collaborative Dual-Branch Unmixing Network for Hyperspectral Images
items.description: Hyperspectral unmixing (HU) based on autoencoders (AEs) is a crucial research task in remote sensing imagery. While existing deep HU networks primarily focus on spatial features, the inherently rich and continuous spectral bands in hyperspectral images (HSIs) harbor significant underutilized information. The intrinsic characteristics of these continuous bands can naturally enable more nuanced and effective modeling of mixed pixels. In this article, we propose the multiview collaborative dual-branch network (MCDB-Net), designed to fully learn and exploit the complex spectral features in high-dimensional hyperspectral data, thereby enhancing the representation capabilities of these features. MCDB-Net constructs a novel multiview spectral block to strengthen the correlation between multiple views of pixel spectra. The full-view spectral feature extraction module highlights important spectral features, while the local multiview spectral feature extraction module provides a detailed understanding of the interactions between multiview spectral information. The multiview abundance collaboration module collaboratively learns spectral feature information from different perspectives and dynamically adjusts the weights of abundance estimations, leading to better integration of abundance features across various views. Extensive experiments on different datasets demonstrate that MCDB-Net achieves higher continuity and robustness in unmixing results, showcasing its powerful capability in spectral feature extraction.

items.title: CentralGraphFormer: Center-Guided Spectral–Spatial Graph Transformer for Hyperspectral Image Classification
items.description: The hyperspectral image (HSI) classification requires the effective exploitation of spectral–spatial information under high spectral redundancy, spatial heterogeneity, and limited labeled samples. Existing CNN- and Transformer-based methods often treat surrounding pixels uniformly and rely on dense attention or shallow fusion strategies, which are poorly aligned with the inherently center-focused supervision of patch-based classification and incur high computational cost. To address these issues, we propose CentralGraphFormer, a center-guided spectral–spatial representation framework that explicitly aligns feature learning and global reasoning with the central-pixel decision objective. The framework integrates three stages: 1) a lightweight spectral shift separable network (S3-Net) for efficient spectral continuity modeling and redundancy suppression; 2) a spatial relevance screening mechanism that adaptively selects semantically consistent neighbors via stochastic gating and biologically inspired smoothing; and 3) a central graph attention module (CGAM) that performs sparse, center-anchored global reasoning using graph-aware keys and a single center query, avoiding the dense self-attention. Extensive experiments on four benchmark HSI datasets demonstrate that CentralGraphFormer consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods while maintaining favorable computational efficiency. Ablation studies further confirm the effectiveness and complementarity of the proposed center-guided spectral, spatial, and global modeling components.

items.title: Context-Reinforced Random-Field Ensembles for Arbitrary-Resolution Hyperspectral Pansharpening
items.description: Arbitrary-resolution hyperspectral (ARHS) pansharpening (PNN) uses high-resolution panchromatic (PAN) images to sharpen low spatial resolution HS (LRHS) images to any desired resolutions which may be far beyond the PAN resolution. In contrast, standard hyperspectral (HS) PNN seeks to pansharpen LRHS images to high spatial resolution HS (HRHS) images merely in the PAN resolution. ARHS PNN brings about new challenges for the HS PNN technique, such as PNN scale generalization and PAN-resolution mismatching. In this work, we propose a novel context-reinforced random-field (CR2F) ensemble paradigm for ARHS PNN implicit neural representation (INR), which is able to form strong coordinate-related ensemble feature representation to improve PNN scale generalization and spectral–spatial reconstruction. Then, following the CR2F ensemble paradigm, we further design two instantiated ARHS PNN INRs, i.e., CR2F-INR1 and CR2F-INR2. Experimental results from three datasets verify the excellent performance of our designs.

items.title: HGA2-FSL: A Heterogeneous Graph Aware-Aggregation Driven Few-Shot Learning Network for Hyperspectral Image Change Detection
items.description: Hyperspectral image (HSI) provides reliable data support for repeated observations of the overlap area through fine spectral reflectance data from numerous bands, enabling accurate capture of regional variation characteristics. However, the vast spectral and spatial information in HSI makes manual annotation laborious and complex. Practical applications thus demand models that achieve high performance with minimal labeled training data. Pay attention to this practical need, we propose a heterogeneous graph aware-aggregation driven few-shot learning (FSL) network (HGA2-FSL). This network enhances model representation through flexible graph construction and aims to improve the accuracy of hyperspectral change detection (CD) under limited labeling by transferring change priors learned from other images. Specifically, we first design a correlation aggregation module (CAM) to build multilevel graph structures that incorporate various types of geographic feature relationships, promoting effective capture and aware-aggregation of local and long-range information. In addition, through joint FSL on very-high-resolution image (VHRI) and HSI, the method utilizes the abundant labeled samples from VHRI and transfers learnable information, reducing the need for labeled samples of HSI. Meanwhile, we design a cross-domain node update-based domain adaptation (DA) method to explore a subspace that minimizes distribution differences, thereby reducing the modality gap between VHRI and HSI and improving the transfer learning performance. Extensive experiments on three public HSI-CD datasets validate the superior performance of HGA2-FSL. The code will be made publicly available at: https://github.com/lsylnnu/HGA2-FSL

items.title: Grouped Attention-Based Spectral–Spatial Feature Learning for Collaborative Hyperspectral and LiDAR Classification
items.description: The attention mechanism, through its dynamic weight allocation and feature enhancement, effectively improves the representation capability of land-cover features in hyperspectral imaging and light detection and ranging (LiDAR) data. However, most implementations of attention mechanisms tend to neglect the local attributes of land-cover features and the prior information inherent in hyperspectral imagery (HSI) data. Grouped feature learning mechanisms can focus on different characteristics or structures of land-cover objects. Based on this, this article integrates a grouping mechanism into the convolutional neural networks (CNNs)-Transformer framework and proposes a grouped attention-based spectral–spatial feature learning (GAS2-FL) network. Exploiting the low-rank prior of HSI data, the network incorporates a spectral–spatial feature learning module and embeds a grouped feature learning strategy to model spectral information interactions among heterogeneous features. Furthermore, a grouped token mechanism and a nonlocal token learning mechanism are developed to enhance the interaction of local attribute features and the learning of fused representations. The superior performance of the proposed network on four HSI and LiDAR classification benchmarks comprehensively demonstrates that its grouped feature learning mechanism is highly effective at extracting and representing the discriminative features essential for land-cover characterization. The source codes will be available at https://github.com/RSIP-NJUPT/GAS2-FL

items.title: DF-PEM: Dual-Flow Prompt-Expert Mamba for Multimodal Remote Sensing Incremental Classification
items.description: Existing deep learning-based multimodal remote sensing imagery (MRSI) classification (MRSIC) models rely on fixed-category paradigms and struggle to adapt to novel categories, primarily due to the catastrophic forgetting of vintage knowledge, which substantially impedes their practical applications. To overcome this challenge, we propose a novel dual-flow prompt-expert Mamba (DF-PEM) network for MRSI incremental classification (IC), which incorporates dedicated parallel branches for spectral and spatial feature extraction, synergized with a cross-modal fusion module to integrate modality-specific representations. The primary objective of DF-PEM is to capture discriminative MRSI features while preserving knowledge of previously seen categories during the incremental learning process. Specifically, DF-PEM integrates the prompt-driven assistant-expert (PAE) mechanism within the Mamba architecture to dynamically activate category-specific prompt experts per input, enabling seamless adaptation to emerging categories while mitigating knowledge erosion of prior classes. Furthermore, a spherical Gaussian sift (SGS) strategy is developed in the initial stage, which models the complex feature distributions of historical categories and neutralizes noise and outlier effects, yielding robust representative prototypes. Finally, a prototype-aware regularization classifier (PRC) that adaptively balances prediction bias between incremental and old categories by learning regularization coefficients, which strategically penalize parameter updates that deviate the model from historical knowledge, further enhancing knowledge retention and generalization. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed DF-PEM significantly outperforms existing methods, validating its effectiveness for MRSI classification tasks.

items.title: Modeling Ancient Shu Road Relics of China Through Fisheye-Adaptive 3-D Gaussian Splatting Reconstruction Framework
items.description: The Ancient Shu Roads constitute a significant historical and cultural heritage attesting to the economic and humanistic interactions between China’s ancient central plains and the Ba-Shu regions. To achieve the digital preservation and management of the Ancient Shu Road relics, it is necessary to conduct 3-D reconstruction to obtain their photorealistic models. However, these relics are typically located in dense forests and cliffs, under such occluded environments, conventional visual 3-D reconstruction methods fail to meet the high-fidelity requirements of cultural heritage digitization. The recently emerged 3-D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) approach shows potential for real-scene reconstruction in complex environments, but its original pipeline follows pinhole camera model, making it unsuitable for fisheye images with severe distortion. To address these challenges, we propose a fisheye-adaptive 3DGS framework for modeling realistic scenes: First, a visual-inertial structure-from-motion (SfM) method is employed to recover real-scale sparse geometry initialization; Next, we introduce a hybrid distortion field and an octahedron projection model into 3DGS, which enables joint optimization of lens distortion and scene representation parameters, thereby remarkably suppressing the rendering artifacts caused by fisheye distortion and building high-fidelity 3-D models. We collected a close-range dataset with handheld devices across several representative Ancient Shu Road heritages, upon which we conducted comprehensive evaluation of our method, validating its superiority in 3-D reconstruction tasks under occluded environments, and offering a viable new solution for cultural heritage digital preservation.

items.title: Unsupervised Knowledge Distillation for Satellite Multiview Stereo With Uncertainty-Aware Supervision
items.description: This article proposes an unsupervised knowledge distillation (KD) framework for satellite multiview stereo (MVS) reconstruction under label-free settings. A teacher–student paradigm is adopted, where a teacher MVS network is first trained using self-supervised multiview geometric constraints, including photometric consistency, feature similarity, smoothness, and structural similarity. The teacher produces multiview height predictions, and geometry-aware uncertainty is inferred from cross-view consistency during multiview fusion. Based on the fused height estimates and uncertainty cues, reliable pseudo-labels are constructed in the form of expectation-based height maps, pixel-wise uncertainty maps, and visibility masks. These pseudo-labels supervise a lightweight student network through probability-volume distillation, combined with uncertainty-weighted height regression and cross-view geometric consistency constraints. Extensive experiments on representative satellite benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves competitive accuracy among unsupervised methods while significantly reducing computational cost and eliminating the need for LiDAR ground truth or pretrained models, providing a scalable solution for large-scale satellite 3-D reconstruction.

items.title: Geospatial Prior Guided Confused-Class Data Augmentation for Semantic Segmentation of Remote Sensing Images
items.description: Semantic segmentation of high spatial resolution remote sensing images plays a crucial role in diverse applications. Deep learning-based methods have emerged as the dominant approach in this field. However, existing methods face the challenge of effectively using the information in annotated training data, resulting in limited model performance. Data augmentation is a commonly used technique to better reveal the information embedded in the data through appropriate transformations. However, these methods usually fail to account for the unique characteristics of remote sensing images, such as the high spectral similarity among different classes and intraclass variation among distinct objects. This oversight hinders the model’s ability to distinguish between spectrally similar classes, resulting in persistent misclassifications. To address these challenges, we propose a novel geospatial prior guided confused-class data augmentation (GCA) method for semantic segmentation of remote sensing images. By emphasizing the occurrence of confused classes within augmented training data, GCA compels the model to focus on learning discriminative features to improve class separability. GCA consists of three key modules: the geospatial prior information extraction module (module  $\mathbf {\boldsymbol {G}}$ ), the confused-class similar units detection module (module  $\mathbf {\boldsymbol {C}}$ ), and the confused-class data augmentation module (module  $\mathbf {\boldsymbol {A}}$ ). Specifically, module  $\mathbf {\boldsymbol {G}}$  extracts geographic units and their spatial relationships. Module  $\mathbf {\boldsymbol {C}}$  identifies highly similar units from confused classes that are prone to misclassification. Module  $\mathbf {\boldsymbol {A}}$  generates challenging training data by emphasizing confused-class similar units under the guidance of geospatial priors. Experiments on the Gaofen Image Dataset (GID) and LoveDA datasets demonstrate that the proposed GCA method shows a better performance than state-of-the-art data augmentation methods. The GCA code is publicly available at https://github.com/Jingying-Li/GCA

items.title: GU-GS: Gaussian Splatting-Based Geometry Refinement and Uncertainty-Aware Learning Method for DSM Generation From Satellite Imagery
items.description: The 3-D reconstruction from multitemporal satellite imagery is a critical task. While 3-D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) has emerged as an efficient alternative to neural radiance field (NeRF)-based methods, its direct application to satellite data often produces geometric noise and artifacts (e.g., floaters and blurry surfaces) and is highly sensitive to illumination and shadow changes, hindering high-fidelity digital surface model (DSM) extraction. To address these limitations, we introduce GU-GS, a Gaussian splatting-based geometry refinement (GR) and uncertainty-aware learning (UAL) method for accurate and efficient DSM generation from satellite imagery. GR module employs a significance-guided pruning strategy to remove redundant Gaussian primitives and leverages opacity entropy regularization to eliminate blurry and unstable surfaces. Through this process, we construct a compact and geometrically consistent primitive set, thus reducing the geometric noise. UAL module leverages a predictor based on semantic features to identify unreliable regions caused by multitemporal illumination and shadow changes and generates an uncertainty mask. By dynamically down-weighting these regions’ contribution to the photometric loss, it effectively filters the supervision signal during the training process, thereby enhancing the stability of optimization and the accuracy of geometric reconstruction. Experiments on the DFC2019 and IARPA2016 datasets demonstrate that our method generates high-precision DSMs, exhibiting superior performance in both accuracy and training speed compared to existing approaches. Compared with Sat-NeRF, our method achieves an average accuracy improvement of 11% and a training speedup of  $40\times $ ; relative to EOGS, it shows an average accuracy enhancement of 24% and a training speed improvement of  $1.8\times $ . Code will be available at: https://github.com/thessshy/GU-GS

items.title: Real-Time Oriented Object Detection Transformer in Remote Sensing Images
items.description: Recent real-time detection transformers (DETRs) have gained popularity due to their simplicity and efficiency. However, these detectors do not explicitly model object rotation, especially in remote sensing imagery where objects appear at arbitrary angles, leading to challenges in angle representation, matching cost, and training stability. In this article, we propose a real-time oriented object DETR, the first real-time end-to-end oriented object detector to the best of our knowledge, that addresses the above issues. Specifically, angle distribution refinement (ADR) is proposed to reformulate angle regression as an iterative refinement of probability distributions, thereby capturing the uncertainty of object rotation and providing a more fine-grained angle representation. Then, we incorporate a Chamfer distance cost into bipartite matching, measuring box distance via vertex sets, enabling more accurate geometric alignment and eliminating ambiguous matches. Moreover, we propose oriented contrastive denoising (OCD) to stabilize training and analyze four noise modes. We observe that a ground truth can be assigned to different index queries across different decoder layers, and analyze this issue using the proposed instability metric. We design a series of model variants and experiments to validate the proposed method. Notably, our O2-DFINE-L, O2-RTDETR-R50 and O2-DEIM-R50 achieve 77.73%/78.45%/80.15% AP50 on DOTA1.0 and 132/119/119 FPS on the  2080ti GPU.

items.title: FuzzyCD: A Fuzzy Logic-Integrated Network for Robust Remote Sensing Change Detection With Noisy Labels
items.description: Deep learning-based change detection (CD) has gained popularity in the field of remote sensing. However, most deep learning-based methods share a common limitation on the availability of massive high-quality labeled training data, where noisy labels are inevitably introduced during the annotation process. Noisy labels induce a surge in epistemic uncertainty and aleatoric uncertainty, thereby compromising the CD performance. Existing CD methods overlook the problem of noisy labels and fail to handle inherent uncertainties. To address this limitation, we propose a novel fuzzy logic-integrated network for robust CD with noisy labels, termed FuzzyCD, which integrates fuzzy logic to effectively model the two types of uncertainties (i.e., epistemic uncertainty and aleatoric uncertainty), mitigating the interference of noisy labels. Specifically, an epistemic uncertainty estimation (EUEU) unit is proposed, which treats xor as fuzzy logic for feature fuzzification, thereby enhancing the model’s cognitive capacity. In addition, an aleatoric uncertainty estimation unit (AUEU) is designed, which characterizes aleatoric uncertainty through probabilistic inference. By transforming the input feature space into a fuzzy feature space, the two fuzzy logic units significantly alleviate the negative impact of noisy labels, achieving improved CD performance and enhanced model robustness to noisy labels. Comprehensive experiments on three public CD datasets (e.g., LEVIR-CD, CDD, and WHU-CD) validate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed FuzzyCD compared to other state-of-the-art methods.

items.title: A Wavelength-Dependent Haze Distribution Prior Network for Remote Sensing RGB Image Dehazing
items.description: Haze in remote sensing imagery often exhibits irregular spatial distributions and highly uneven concentrations due to complex atmospheric conditions and large observation scales. Moreover, haze exhibits different scattering and attenuation behaviors across RGB wavelengths. However, most existing dehazing methods are developed under the assumption of spatially uniform haze, which is frequently violated in real remote sensing scenarios. In this article, a wavelength-dependent haze distribution prior dehazing method is proposed, which embeds a haze distribution prior to the dehazing learning process. First, a haze distribution modeling network (HDMNet) is introduced to estimate the wavelength-dependent haze distribution map by jointly modeling atmospheric light and the wavelength-dependent transmission map, where the transmission map serves as an implicit representation of the haze concentration. Furthermore, a multibranch interaction network (MBINet) is designed to integrate the wavelength-dependent haze distribution map into the RGB image dehazing process, enabling effective improvement for haze removal under complex and nonuniform conditions. Finally, a collaborative dehazing loss is designed to guide HDMNet to focus on regions where haze severely degrades image quality, utilizing the residual differences between dehazed RGB images and haze-free RGB images. The proposed method is evaluated on multiple synthetic hazy datasets and a real-world hazy dataset, demonstrating great improvement over state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative metrics and visual quality.

items.title: TSFDet: Task-Specific Feature Disentanglement for Two-Stage Oriented Object Detector
