items.description: Two-stage oriented object detectors exhibit high detection accuracy and hold significant application value in civilian and military domains. However, existing methods suffer from inconsistent prediction results due to feature entanglement between localization and classification tasks, severely constraining detection performance. To address this issue, we propose a task-specific feature disentanglement for a two-stage oriented object detector (TSFDet). Inspired by the neural mechanisms underlying the human visual cognitive system, the method disentangles the features for localization and classification tasks by constructing a dual-branch feature pyramid network (FPN) architecture. An edge-feature guidance network (EFGN) is designed for the localization branch, which extracts target edge-gradient features using the Sobel operator and enhances contour modeling capability through adaptive weighted fusion. A multi-level context-feature enhancement network (MCEN) is constructed for the classification branch, leveraging graph convolutional networks (GCNs) to model global semantic relationships for focusing on salient target regions. Simultaneously, a feature interaction module (FIM) is designed to achieve spatial alignment of the dual branches and complementary feature fusion by learning offset maps. Finally, a two-stage oriented-decoupling detection head (TODH) is employed to further separate the feature paths for classification and localization. Comprehensive and extensive evaluations on three benchmarks, including DIOR-R, MAR20, and ShipRSImageNet, indicate that TSFDet significantly surpasses existing methods, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

items.title: Polarization Super-Resolution Remote Sensing Imaging Based on Compressed Sensing and Deep Learning
items.description: Remote sensing is widely applied in environmental monitoring, Earth observation, and military reconnaissance, with increasing demands for higher spatial resolution, improved contrast, and multidimensional feature acquisition. Polarization imaging, particularly enabled by division-of-focal-plane (DoFP) polarization detectors, offers advantages in material differentiation and structural enhancement due to its ability to capture intensity, angle, and degree of polarization (DoP) simultaneously in a compact, snapshot configuration. However, current research and applications of DoFP-based polarization imaging still encounter several key challenges: first, spatial resolution degradation and interchannel aliasing arising from pixel-level downsampling and field-of-view (FoV) misalignment; second, the absence of physical priors in most deep learning models, which limits their interpretability and robustness; finally, maintaining image quality under sparse sampling conditions remains a significant technical challenge. To overcome these challenges, we propose polarization compressed sensing generative adversarial network (PCSGAN), a dual-stage polarization super-resolution framework that couples compressed sensing theory with deep generative modeling, enhanced by polarization degradation simulation and sparse regularization. The original DoFP imaging resolution itself is half that of the detector’s pixel scale. In contrast, the proposed method achieves  $4\times $  super-resolution reconstruction with only 6.25% sampling (equivalent to a single snapshot), effectively doubling the native spatial resolution of the detector while achieving high-fidelity polarization information recovery. We validate our approach on three public datasets and one self-collected dataset. Compared with six state-of-the-art methods across 20 types of remote sensing scenes, PCSGAN consistently achieves the best average results, improving peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) by 2.3%–11.7% and structural similarity index (SSIM) by 0.1%–12.8%. The effectiveness of PCSGAN is further demonstrated through uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV)-based remote sensing experiments, showing strong potential for real-time, high-precision polarization imaging applications.

items.title: Evaluation and Verification of Different Characterization Methods of Echo Signal for the AEMS/ACDL
items.description: In view of the strong subjectivity in existing researches regarding the accurate extraction of the echo signal from the aerosol and carbon detection lidar (ACDL) onboard the atmospheric environment monitoring satellite (AEMS), a systematic evaluation of the pulse peak method (PPM), pulse integration method (PIM), and pulse fitting method (PFM) is conducted. Echo signals from four typical geographical regions, namely the plain, mountain, ocean, and plateau, are analyzed to explore the applicability of different signal extraction methods under varying peak intensities and signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs). The differential absorption optical depth (DAOD) calculated by the PIM exhibits higher stability and smaller standard deviation than those obtained using the PPM and PFM, indicating that the PIM is more suitable for most geographical regions. In order to reduce the errors introduced by the uncertainties of meteorological data, a self-verification approach based on the micro-region stability assumption is proposed as the evaluation index of comparing the performance of three signal extraction schemes, providing a practical solution when the external verification data are unavailable. Computer simulations further demonstrate that the number of integration points for achieving the maximum SNR is inversely proportional to the mean SNR of the signal, offering a quantitative guidance for enhancing echo signal quality through appropriate integration points selection. The inversion accuracy of the XCO2 obtained using different signal extraction methods is evaluated, and the PIM achieves the smallest XCO2 deviation, with an average deviation of −0.43 ppm compared with the XCO2 data observed by the global total carbon column observing Network (TCCON) at the Xianghe Station. This study provides a practical, efficient, and robust technical framework for the XCO2 inversion of the new generation lidar satellite AEMS together with offering the valuable technical support for the global CO2 monitoring applications.

items.title: How Effective Are Time-Series Models for Precipitation Nowcasting? A Comprehensive Benchmark for GNSS-Based Precipitation Nowcasting
items.description: Precipitation Nowcasting, which aims to predict precipitation within the next 0–6 h, is critical for disaster mitigation and real-time response planning. However, most time-series forecasting benchmarks in meteorology are evaluated on variables with strong periodicity, such as temperature and humidity, which fail to reflect model capabilities in more complex and practically meteorology scenarios like precipitation nowcasting. To address this gap, we propose RainfallBench a benchmark designed for precipitation nowcasting, a highly challenging and practically relevant task characterized by zero inflation, temporal decay, and nonstationarity, focusing on predicting precipitation within the next 0–6 h. The dataset is derived from five years of meteorological observations, recorded at hourly intervals across six essential variables, and collected from more than 140 Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) stations globally. In particular, it incorporates precipitable water vapor (PWV), a crucial indicator of precipitation that is absent in other datasets. We further design specialized evaluation protocols to assess model performance on key meteorological challenges, including multiscale prediction, multiresolution forecasting, and extreme precipitation events, benchmarking 17 state-of-the-art models across six major architectures on RainfallBench. Additionally, to address the zero-inflation and temporal decay issues overlooked by existing models, we introduce bi-focus precipitation forecaster (BFPF), a plug-and-play module that incorporates domain-specific priors to enhance precipitation nowcasting. Statistical analysis and ablation studies validate the comprehensiveness of our dataset as well as the effectiveness of our methodology. Code and datasets are available at https://github.com/yfangZhang/RainfallBench

items.title: Unlocking Shallow Subsurface Architecture in Coastal Zones: Integrated ESPAC-Genetic Algorithm Inversion With Sparse Drilling Constraints
items.description: High-resolution shear-wave velocity (Vs) characterization is essential for mitigating seismic hazards and enhancing infrastructure resilience in coastal megacities; however, conventional active-source methods often prove impractical in soft-sediment, infrastructure-dense environments. This article presents a borehole-constrained extended spatial autocorrelation-genetic algorithm (ESPAC-GA) workflow that integrates sparse microtremor arrays with minimal drilling investment to achieve robust 2-D Vs imaging to 50 m in depth. On the western Pacific coastal plain, a ten-node nested triangular array (58-m aperture) was deployed along a 560-m transect, constrained by three 60-m boreholes serving as constraints or for validation. Hyperparameters (population: 20 and generations: 40) were optimized through 50 Monte Carlo runs, and ensemble averaging of five independent inversions effectively suppressed nonuniqueness. Numerical validation demonstrates layer thickness and Vs errors of approximately 3%, whereas field application—characterized by highly attenuative, water-saturated clays—reveals a characteristic “shallow-sensitive, deep-robust” response. The resulting 2-D Vs profile clearly delineates the marine–lacustrine–tuff sequence and laterally variable bedrock interfaces, with cumulative bedrock depth errors remaining below 6% and bedrock velocity errors of merely −6.9%. This accuracy meets offshore wind foundation and immersed-tunnel engineering specifications while reducing drilling costs by over 30%. Furthermore, the optimized hyperparameters may serve as a useful initial model for analogous deltaic settings worldwide. This optimized workflow offers a cost-effective, scalable tool for real-time, high-resolution Vs mapping in coastal zones, supporting climate-adaptive urban planning and infrastructure risk assessment.

items.title: Viscoacoustic Least-Squares Reverse Time Migration Using Structure-Oriented Total Variation Norm Regularization
items.description: Viscoacoustic least-squares reverse time migration (QLSRTM) has emerged as a cutting-edge imaging tool, which can overcome the intrinsic attenuation effects of subsurface media and provide a robust solution for reconstructing the true reflectivity of subsurface. However, the migrated image of QLSRTM generally have side-effects mainly caused by the inaccurate background velocity model, incomplete acquisition geometry, inadequate physical modeling assumptions, and so on. Due to the excellent edge-preserving denoising capability, the total variation (TV) norm regularization has been introduced into the least-squares inversion framework to suppress the side-effects and give a segmented smooth solution. Nevertheless, conventional TV norm constraint solely considers the gradient variation of inversion parameter along the horizontal and vertical directions, which might reduce its adaptability for complex structures. For this reason, we propose a QLSRTM algorithm that integrates a structure-oriented TV norm regularization into the objective function. Specifically, the decoupled fractional Laplacians (DFLs) viscoacoustic wave equation is utilized to accurately characterize the propagation effects of seismic waves in subsurface media. Besides the structural directional information are extracted from the inverted image through gradient structure tensor (GST) method within each iteration and then incorporated into the conventional TV norm to constraint inversion. In this article, we adopted the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMMs) to iteratively solve the constraint structure-oriented TV norm minimization problem. The feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed approach are validated through two synthetic and a field data. Migration results demonstrate that the proposed approach can not only compensate for attenuation effects effectively and minimize the migration artifacts significantly, but also obtain a better quality for imaging complex structures than conventional regularization.

items.title: Magnetic Target Boundary Identification Using L1 Norm Regularized Inversion and Optimal Slice Selection
items.description: The identification of magnetic target boundaries from measured field data is a key research area in geophysics. However, existing methods based on magnetic field components or gradient tensors exhibit limitations in their identification effectiveness. To address this deficiency, this study proposes an L1 norm regularized inversion method based on the magnetic moment gradient. Specifically, the method projects the 3-D target onto a 2-D plane and formulates an objective function that leverages the magnetic moment gradient with L1 norm regularization. It then introduces a novel section selection method, which combines a coarse-to-fine strategy with an analysis of fitting term residual variations. This method first generates candidate sections via the coarse-to-fine strategy and then identifies a turning point from the differences in the fitting term residuals across the sections. This point signifies the inversion’s transition from rapid change to stable convergence, thereby determining a robust inversion section. Furthermore, a benchmark-adaptive method for re-weighting the regularization parameter is introduced, which obviates the need for its independent calculation for each section. We further propose rank-based normalization of the inversion results to balance the responses from both strong and weak anomalies. Results from both simulations and field experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves better performance in boundary identification than existing methods.
